  </Panel.Block>
</Panel>

accessibility:
- The root panel renders as a semantic `
`, a navigation landmark, by default. For a panel that is not navigation, set `as` to `article`, `section`, `aside` or `div`, and give a `section` an accessible name (for example `aria-labelledby` pointing at the `Panel.Heading`'s `id`) if it should be a region. - `Panel.Heading` renders Bulma's `

`, which assistive tech reads as a plain paragraph: it isn't a heading, and it doesn't name the panel. A screen reader user who moves by heading skips it, and one who moves by landmark hears "navigation" for each panel with nothing to tell them apart. Give the heading `role="heading"` and the `aria-level` that fits the headings already on the page. To name a `nav` panel, the default, after its heading, give the heading an `id` that's unique on the page and write `aria-labelledby` with that id on the `Panel`, the way the bullet above names a `section`. The examples above name each panel this way, and the first also makes its heading one. - The `Panel.Block` by default renders as an anchor ``. Its props follow `as`: only an `a` takes the anchor attributes (`href`, `target`, `download` and the rest), and only a `label` takes `htmlFor` and `form`. A block on another tag drops them, and `rel`, at runtime too. - Give each `Panel.Block` that opens something an `href`, as the examples do: an `` with no `href` isn't a link, so Tab skips it, Enter does nothing on it, and assistive tech reads it as text. A block that isn't a link takes `as="div"`, or `as="label"` around a control. The links you write in `Panel.Tabs` take an `href` too, and the active one `aria-current="true"` beside its `is-active` class, which is only seen. - `Panel.InputBlock`'s field takes its name from its `placeholder`, which browsers fall back to, and an `aria-label` you pass it names nothing. [A Search Field With a Name of Its Own](https://bestax.io/docs/api/components/panel#a-search-field-with-a-name-of-its-own) shows what to pass and how to build a field with a name of its own. - `Panel.Block active` sets `aria-current="page"` on the element `as` renders, the `` by default, so the current block isn't only a color. An `aria-current` you pass wins: a panel of sections on one page can say `"location"`, and `aria-current={false}` turns it off, as on an active `label` block with a checkbox. - A panel with no `color` keeps its heading readable on the dark scheme through bestax's `components/panel` partial, which `extras.css` and `bestax.css` include. Bulma's CSS alone writes that heading white on light gray. - A panel with a `color` draws the text of its active block and active tab, the active block's icon and the active tab's underline in that color at the lightness Bulma picks for the color's text on the page, through the same partial, so they read on both schemes. Black takes the title text's lightness, which is white on the dark scheme. Without the partial the text inherits the color's text helper Panel puts on the panel, and the icon and underline take the color's own lightness, which for a light or white panel is near white on white. - **Forced colors:** Bulma marks the active tab and the active block with colors alone, which forced colors (Windows' contrast themes) replaces, so bestax's styles draw a bar in the system's highlight color there: along the bottom of the active tab, and down the start edge of the active block. The tab, the block and everything in them stay in the contrast theme's colors. It reads the `is-active` class, on a `Panel.Block` and on the tab links you write in `Panel.Tabs`. The panel's own edge is a shadow, which forced colors drops, so the same styles draw it as a one pixel line in the system's text color around the panel, with a line under the heading in place of its fill. This comes from the same partial.
summary: The `Panel` component implements Bulma's versatile panel block for React.

parts.summary: The `Panel` component implements Bulma's versatile panel block for React.

props.name: as
props.description: HTML element to render (default: `nav`). A `nav` is a `navigation` landmark, which suits a panel of links; a panel that is not navigation takes another tag. Bulma's own colored panels use `article`. A `section` is a `region` landmark only once it has an accessible name, such as `aria-labelledby` pointing at the `id` of its `Panel.Heading`.

props.name: color
props.description: Bulma color modifier for the panel. With none, the heading takes the text color, with its title in the page background's color so it reads on both schemes. On the dark scheme that title color comes from bestax's stylesheets: Bulma's CSS alone writes it white on light gray there. With a color, the active block's and active tab's text, the active block's icon and the active tab's underline take it at the lightness Bulma picks for the color's text on the page, also from bestax's stylesheets, so they read on both schemes. Black takes the title text's lightness, which is white on the dark scheme. With a `colorShade`, the text takes that shade and the icon and underline the color's own lightness, as Bulma draws them.

parts.summary:
The panel's title: a paragraph to assistive tech, until you give it `role="heading"` and an `aria-level`. It renders Bulma's `

`, which doesn't name the panel either. Pick the level that fits the headings already on the page, so screen reader users can move to it by heading. To name the panel after it, give it an `id` that's unique on the page and write `aria-labelledby` with that id on the `Panel`: two `nav` panels, the default, are then two navigation landmarks a screen reader can tell apart.

parts.summary: Individual panel block (renders as `<a class="panel-block">` unless `as` says otherwise). Give a block that opens something an `href`: an `<a>` with no `href` isn't a link, so Tab skips it. A block that isn't a link takes `as="div"`, or `as="label"` around a control.

props.name: as
props.description: HTML element to render (default: `a`). Bulma styles a `label` block as clickable, like an `a`, and a `div` block as static content, such as a table. The props follow the tag, so the anchor attributes (`href`, `target`, `download` and the rest) are typed only on an `a` and `htmlFor` only on a `label`; at runtime the block also drops them, and `rel`, on the other tags. `Panel.CheckboxBlock`, `Panel.InputBlock` and `Panel.ButtonBlock` render the usual `label` and `div` blocks with their contents.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes.

props.name: active
props.description: Marks the block as the current one. It adds Bulma's `is-active` class, and `aria-current="page"` on the element `as` renders, so assistive tech can tell which block is current too. An `aria-current` you pass wins, even `undefined`: use it to say something else (`"location"` for a section of one page, say), or `aria-current={false}` to turn it off, as on an active block that isn't navigation, such as a `label` with a checkbox.

props.name: children
props.description: Block content.

parts.catchAll: Remaining props of the element selected by as (default <a>)

parts.summary: Icon wrapper with panel styling (renders as `<span class="panel-icon">`, containing an `<i/>` when a `name` is given, or the custom node passed as `children`). Accepts all Icon props (`name`, `variant`, `features`, etc.), or `children` for a custom node.

props.name: name
props.description: The icon name, with or without its library prefix (e.g. `'star'` or `'fa-star'`). Mutually exclusive with `children`.

props.name: children
props.description: A custom node (an inline SVG, a `react-icons` component, …) rendered inside the icon container in place of a class-based glyph. Mutually exclusive with `name`.

props.name: icon
props.description: Legacy icon class string (e.g. `'fas fa-star'`). Only its last segment is read, as the glyph name; the library still comes from `library` or `ConfigProvider`, so `'mdi mdi-rocket'` renders an `fa` class unless the effective library is already `mdi` — set it here or on the provider.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes to apply.

props.name: textColor
props.description: Text color helper.

props.name: color
props.description: Text color alias: renders `has-text-<color>`, exactly like `textColor`. Not a filled variant (no `.icon.is-<color>` CSS exists). Prefer `textColor`, which takes precedence when both are set; use `bgColor` for a colored surface.

props.name: bgColor
props.description: Background color helper.

props.name: library
props.description: The icon library to use ('fa' = Font Awesome, 'mdi' = Material Design Icons, 'ion' = Ionicons Web Components, 'material-icons' = Google Material Icons, 'material-symbols' = Google Material Symbols). Defaults to the value set in ConfigProvider or 'fa' if not configured. Ignored when `children` supplies the glyph instead of `name`.

props.name: variant
props.description: Icon style variant (e.g. `'solid'`, `'outlined'`, `'rounded'`). Ignored when `children` supplies the glyph instead of `name`.

props.name: features
props.description: Additional modifiers (e.g. `'fa-lg'`, `'fa-spin'`, `'is-size-1'`). Ignored when `children` supplies the glyph instead of `name`.

props.name: libraryFeatures
props.description: Additional modifiers in the older combined form, parsed into `variant` and `features`.

props.name: size
props.description: Size modifier for the icon container.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.description: Accessible name for an icon that means something on its own. Set it and the container span gets `role="img"` with this `aria-label`, so the name is exactly this text: a Material ligature such as `rocket_launch` inside stays out of it. Leave it unset (or empty) and the icon is decorative: the span renders `aria-hidden="true"` and no name, so it adds nothing to the accessible name of a `Button` or text around it. For an icon-only control, put the name on the control (e.g. `Button`'s `aria-label`) and leave this unset. A non-empty native `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` passed instead also counts as a name, and an explicit `role` or `aria-hidden` wins over both defaults. An unnamed icon given a `role` or a `tabIndex` of its own isn't hidden, since hiding something focusable is a failure of its own, so give it a name. For Ionicons the `<ion-icon>` inside is always `aria-hidden`, so it adds no image of its own.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline style object.

parts.summary: Search input with icon (renders as `<div class="panel-block">` around the `<input>`). Its field takes its name from its `placeholder`, which browsers fall back to, and has none without one, so pass one that says what it searches. Attributes you pass for the field, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` and `id` among them, go on the `div`, not on the `<input>`, and name nothing there. For a field that needs a name of its own, an `id` or other input attributes, build the block from `<Panel.Block as="div">` with a `Control` and an `Input` inside.
